changes: First release of Downloader Bot, based on WD-40
/download searches for a song and sends it as an MP3 (192 kbps, with title, artist, album and cover art tags)
Search by name or paste a link from YouTube, SoundCloud, Deezer, Spotify, Apple Music and more
When searching by name, pick the source and the exact track from a list
Spotify and Apple Music links are matched to a source that can be downloaded
Files too big for the server's upload limit can be sent as a compressed version instead
Downloaded files are cached and cleared every day at 3 AM
The startup version check now compares with the version on GitHub
New activity statuses
Google Drive support: /drive login links your Drive, /drive logout unlinks it, /drive status shows the linked account, storage and what was saved
When your Drive is linked, /download asks whether to send the file here or save it to Drive
Files too big for Discord can now be saved to Google Drive, on top of the compressed version
Playlists and albums can be downloaded as a zip (with a playlist.m3u8), saved to Google Drive. Up to 100 tracks, with a progress bar and a cancel button
New formats: MP3, M4A (AAC), Opus and FLAC, in low, medium or high quality. Use the format and quality options of /download
New /drive settings command: choose where downloads go (ask, always Drive, always Discord) and your default format and quality
/download now has a 10 second cooldown
Up to 3 playlists can download at the same time across all users
Fixed a song failing to download again after the daily cleanup
Fixed YouTube downloads waiting about a minute and logging errors at the end of a song
YouTube streams that cut off early now fail instead of sending an incomplete file
Added a privacy policy
Self-hosting: a SQLite database is now used (created automatically at ./data/bot.db, or DATABASE_PATH) and checked at startup
Self-hosting: new GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and GOOGLE_DRIVE_TOKEN_KEY variables for Google Drive
Self-hosting: new SUPERUSER_MODE variable (on or off) to override superuser mode, and the startup log now says why it's on or off
Self-hosting: commands can now reply privately, /drive replies are only visible to you
